types.embedding_query_text: Organization: A structured group of people with a particular purpose, such as a business, government department, or charity. Also called Company, Firm, Corporation, Agency. Examples: Samsung Electronics, Nvidia, Counterpoint Research, IDC.

chosen_type.label: Organization
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org Organization class directly matches the OIE_TYPE definition and all mentions are clear examples of organizations.

candidates.label: Organization
candidates.comment: An Organization is a group of people with a particular purpose, such as a school, NGO, corporation, or club. Also called entity, institution, association. Examples: Google, Harvard University, Red Cross, a local sports club. Distinct from Person, which is an individual.

candidates.label: Corporation
candidates.comment: A Corporation is a legal entity separate from its owners, typically formed for business purposes. Also called company, incorporated business, limited company. Examples: Apple Inc., Google LLC, Microsoft Corporation, Coca-Cola Company. Distinct from Cooperative, which is an organization owned and operated by its members for their mutual benefit.

candidates.label: ResearchOrganization
candidates.comment: A ResearchOrganization is an Organization dedicated to conducting research. Also called scientific institute, research company, academic research center. Examples: Max Planck Society, Bell Labs, a university research department, a pharmaceutical research firm.

candidates.label: Consortium
candidates.comment: A membership organization typically composed of other organizations collaborating on a shared project or goal. Also called alliance, syndicate, federation, partnership. Examples: World Wide Web Consortium (W3C), a research consortium, a banking consortium, a joint venture. Distinct from Organization, which is a general grouping of people or entities.

candidates.label: SearchRescueOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization dedicated to finding and providing aid to people who are lost or in imminent danger. Also called SAR team, rescue service, emergency search unit. Examples: a mountain rescue team, a coast guard search and rescue unit, a volunteer SAR group.

types.embedding_query_text: FinancialMetric: A quantifiable measure used to assess the financial performance or health of an entity. Also called Financial indicator, Economic measure, Performance indicator, Fiscal metric. Examples: profits, Sales, Stock Market Value, Record Quarterly Sales.

chosen_type.label: FinancialMetric
chosen_type.definition: A quantifiable measure used to assess the financial performance or health of an entity.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class directly represents a category of financial performance measures. QuantitativeValue is the closest parent as these are measurable values.

candidates.label: FinancialIncentive
candidates.comment: A FinancialIncentive is an Intangible representing financial benefits offered for goods or services, including details like amount, status, and eligibility criteria. Also called rebate, subsidy, grant, discount. Examples: A government tax credit for electric vehicles, a manufacturer's rebate on an appliance, a low-interest loan program, a student scholarship.

candidates.label: MedicalRiskScore
candidates.comment: A medical risk estimator that is a simple system summing risk factors to yield a score associated with prognosis. Also called clinical score, prognostic score, risk index. Examples: "CHAD score", "TIMI risk score", "APACHE II score". Distinct from MedicalRiskCalculator, which involves more complex mathematical calculations.

candidates.label: MonetaryAmount
candidates.comment: A structured value representing a monetary value or range, typically expressed with a currency. Also called amount of money, financial value, currency amount. Examples: "$50 USD", "£1,000 to £1,000,000 GBP", "€25.99". Distinct from PriceSpecification, which describes the price of an offer.

candidates.label: QuantitativeValue
candidates.comment: A QuantitativeValue is a StructuredValue representing a point value or interval for product characteristics or other purposes. Also called numerical value, measurable value. Examples: a product's weight of '5 kg', a temperature range of '20-25°C', a height of '1.8 meters', a price of '$99.99'. Distinct from QualitativeValue, which represents a predefined, non-numeric value.

candidates.label: MedicalRiskCalculator
candidates.comment: A medical risk estimator that is a complex mathematical calculation, often requiring an online tool, used to assess prognosis. Also called prognosis calculator, risk assessment tool, clinical prediction model. Examples: a calculator for cardiovascular disease risk, a tool for predicting cancer recurrence. Distinct from MedicalRiskScore, which is a simpler sum of risk factors.

types.embedding_query_text: Percentage: A rate, number, or amount in each hundred. Also called Rate, Proportion, Ratio, Fraction. Examples: 1,800%, Almost 7%, More than 200%, More than 80%.

chosen_type.label: Quantity
chosen_type.justification: A percentage is a measurable amount, making schema.org Quantity the most appropriate general data type for this concept.

candidates.label: MonetaryAmount
candidates.comment: A structured value representing a monetary value or range, typically expressed with a currency. Also called amount of money, financial value, currency amount. Examples: "$50 USD", "£1,000 to £1,000,000 GBP", "€25.99". Distinct from PriceSpecification, which describes the price of an offer.

candidates.label: Quantity
candidates.comment: Quantity is a data type representing measurable amounts such as distance, time, mass, or weight. Also called amount, measure, magnitude. Examples: '3 kg', '4 milligrams', '10 meters', '2 hours'.

candidates.label: ExchangeRateSpecification
candidates.comment: An ExchangeRateSpecification is a StructuredValue representing details about an exchange rate. Also called currency exchange rate, foreign exchange rate. Examples: The exchange rate between USD and EUR, a specific conversion rate for a financial transaction, details including fees and validity period.

candidates.label: Integer
candidates.comment: Integer is a data type representing a whole number without a fractional component. Also called whole number, natural number (if positive), counting number. Examples: 0, 1, -5, 1000. Distinct from Float, which includes decimal values.

candidates.label: ChemicalSubstance
candidates.comment: A portion of matter with constant composition, composed of molecular entities of the same or different types. Also called chemical compound, chemical, substance, molecule. Examples: Water (H2O), Sodium Chloride (NaCl), Ethanol, Oxygen.

types.embedding_query_text: ProductCategory: A classification of goods or services that share similar characteristics or functions. Also called Product line, Goods type, Service group, Merchandise class. Examples: AI Memory Chips, Semiconductors for Data Centres, AI Infrastructure, Chips for Everyday Electronics.

chosen_type.label: ProductCategory
chosen_type.definition: A classification of products based on their characteristics, uses, or market segments.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class directly represents a classification or category of products. DefinedTerm is a suitable parent for a classification term.

candidates.label: ProductGroup
candidates.comment: A ProductGroup is a Product representing a group of products that vary only in specific attributes like size, color, or material, serving as a template for its variants. Also called product family, product line, variant group. Examples: a specific model of smartphone available in different colors and storage sizes, a t-shirt design available in various sizes and fabrics, a car model with different trim levels. Distinct from Product, which is a specific variant offered for sale.

candidates.label: SomeProducts
candidates.comment: A placeholder representing multiple similar products of the same kind, used when specific individual products are not distinguished. Also called product group, product category, generic products, similar items. Examples: 'a batch of apples', 'several identical t-shirts', 'a collection of standard screws'.

candidates.label: Product
candidates.comment: A Product is any offered good or service. Also called item, merchandise, offering. Examples: a pair of shoes, a concert ticket, a car rental service, an episode of a TV show.

candidates.label: ProductModel
candidates.comment: A ProductModel is a Product representing a datasheet or vendor specification of a prototypical product description. Also called product prototype, product specification, product blueprint. Examples: the technical specifications for a new laptop model, a design document for a car engine, a vendor's product data sheet, a conceptual product design.

candidates.label: CategoryCode
candidates.comment: A defined term representing a specific code within a classification system. Also called classification code, item code, type code. Examples: UNSPSC code for office supplies, NAICS code for manufacturing, a product category ID.

types.embedding_query_text: Multiplier: A factor by which a quantity is multiplied. Also called Factor, Coefficient, Magnification, Increase factor. Examples: 19-fold jump, More than double.

chosen_type.label: Quantity
chosen_type.justification: A multiplier is a numerical factor, which is a type of measurable amount, making schema.org Quantity the best fit.

candidates.label: MedicalRiskFactor
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing anything that increases a person's likelihood of developing a disease, medical condition, or complication. Also called risk element, predisposing factor, vulnerability. Examples: "smoking", "high cholesterol", "family history of heart disease", "obesity". Distinct from MedicalRiskEstimator, which is a tool to calculate risk based on multiple factors.

candidates.label: AggregateOffer
candidates.comment: An AggregateOffer is an Offer that groups multiple individual offers for the same product or service, often from different merchants. Also called bundled offers, collective offer, multiple offers. Examples: A product page showing prices from several retailers, a flight search result listing different airline prices, a comparison shopping result. Distinct from Offer, which represents a single offer for a product or service.

candidates.label: Quantity
candidates.comment: Quantity is a data type representing measurable amounts such as distance, time, mass, or weight. Also called amount, measure, magnitude. Examples: '3 kg', '4 milligrams', '10 meters', '2 hours'.

candidates.label: CompoundPriceSpecification
candidates.comment: A price specification that combines multiple prices applicable for different dimensions of consumption. Also called bundled price, multi-component price, composite pricing. Examples: A utility bill with separate charges for electricity and water, a rental agreement with base rent and a "final cleaning" fee, a software license with per-user and per-feature costs. Distinct from PriceSpecification, which is a general description of a price.

candidates.label: UserPlusOnes
candidates.comment: An outdated type representing a user's interaction of giving a "+1" endorsement, typically on Google+ or similar platforms. Also called user endorsement, +1, social recommendation. Examples: a user giving a +1 to a web page, endorsing a business, recommending content.

types.embedding_query_text: EconomicFactor: A variable or condition that influences economic activity, growth, or stability. Also called Market force, Economic driver, Business condition, Fiscal element. Examples: Demand, Supply, Prices, AI Boom.

chosen_type.label: StatisticalVariable
chosen_type.justification: Economic factors are often measurable variables or conditions, which aligns well with the definition of schema.org StatisticalVariable.

candidates.label: MedicalRiskFactor
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing anything that increases a person's likelihood of developing a disease, medical condition, or complication. Also called risk element, predisposing factor, vulnerability. Examples: "smoking", "high cholesterol", "family history of heart disease", "obesity". Distinct from MedicalRiskEstimator, which is a tool to calculate risk based on multiple factors.

candidates.label: Demand
candidates.comment: An intangible entity representing a public announcement by an organization or person seeking specific goods or services. Also called Request for goods, wanted ad, procurement request, call for bids. Examples: A company seeking bids for a new IT system, a person looking to buy a specific vintage car, a job posting for a software engineer. Distinct from Offer, which is an announcement to provide goods or services.

candidates.label: StatisticalVariable
candidates.comment: A measurable statistical metric that can be observed at a place and time, defined by a population type and specific constraints. Also called statistical metric, data point, observable quantity, measurement variable. Examples: median height of female persons, average temperature in a city, count of news articles published daily. Distinct from StatisticalPopulation, which is the group being measured, not the measurement itself.

candidates.label: BusinessFunction
candidates.comment: A BusinessFunction is an Enumeration specifying the type of activity or access rights offered by an organization through an offer. Also called commercial activity, service type, transaction type. Examples: Sell, LeaseOut, Repair, ProvideService, Buy.

candidates.label: FinancialIncentive
candidates.comment: A FinancialIncentive is an Intangible representing financial benefits offered for goods or services, including details like amount, status, and eligibility criteria. Also called rebate, subsidy, grant, discount. Examples: A government tax credit for electric vehicles, a manufacturer's rebate on an appliance, a low-interest loan program, a student scholarship.

types.embedding_query_text: MonetaryValue: A quantity of money or its equivalent in goods or services. Also called Amount, Sum, Price, Cost. Examples: 89.4tn won, 171tn won, $80bn, $880bn.

chosen_type.label: MonetaryAmount
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org MonetaryAmount class perfectly matches the OIE_TYPE definition and all mentions are specific monetary values.

candidates.label: MonetaryAmount
candidates.comment: A structured value representing a monetary value or range, typically expressed with a currency. Also called amount of money, financial value, currency amount. Examples: "$50 USD", "£1,000 to £1,000,000 GBP", "€25.99". Distinct from PriceSpecification, which describes the price of an offer.

candidates.label: DatedMoneySpecification
candidates.comment: A structured value representing a monetary amount that is valid or applicable over a specified time period, though its use is superseded by MonetaryAmount. Also called Time-bound monetary value, period-specific money, dated financial amount. Examples: An employee's salary from 2022-01-01 to 2022-12-31, a subscription fee valid for a quarter, a bonus paid for a specific fiscal year.

candidates.label: MonetaryAmountDistribution
candidates.comment: A quantitative value distribution representing a statistical distribution of monetary amounts. Also called money distribution, financial range, income distribution. Examples: "average salary range", "distribution of asset values", "price range for a product category".

candidates.label: MonetaryGrant
candidates.comment: An intangible grant that provides a sum of money. Also called financial grant, money award, cash donation. Examples: a research grant, a scholarship, a government subsidy. Distinct from Grant, which can be non-monetary.

candidates.label: QuantitativeValue
candidates.comment: A QuantitativeValue is a StructuredValue representing a point value or interval for product characteristics or other purposes. Also called numerical value, measurable value. Examples: a product's weight of '5 kg', a temperature range of '20-25°C', a height of '1.8 meters', a price of '$99.99'. Distinct from QualitativeValue, which represents a predefined, non-numeric value.

types.embedding_query_text: Date: A specific day, month, and year, or a particular point in time. Also called Day, Calendar date, Specific date, Point in time. Examples: April 1, 2026, June 30, 2026, Tuesday, Start of This Year.

chosen_type.label: Date
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org Date data type is the most direct fit for specific calendar dates and date-related references like 'Tuesday' and 'Start of This Year'.

candidates.label: Date
candidates.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

candidates.label: DateTime
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, combining both date and time components according to ISO 8601. Also called Timestamp, date and time string, ISO 8601 datetime. Examples: "2023-10-27T10:30:00Z", "1999-12-31T23:59:59-05:00", "2024-01-15T14:00:00". Distinct from Date, which only specifies a calendar date without time.

candidates.label: DayOfWeek
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing a specific day of the week, used for scheduling or recurring events. Also called Weekday, calendar day, day name. Examples: Monday, Tuesday, Saturday, Sunday. Distinct from Date, which specifies a particular calendar date.

candidates.label: Time
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, typically in hh:mm:ss format, potentially with a timezone offset. Also called timestamp, clock time, time of day. Examples: "14:30:00", "09:00:00Z", "17:45:30+01:00".

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

types.embedding_query_text: PerformanceMetric: A standard of measurement used to evaluate the effectiveness or success of an action, process, or entity. Also called Performance indicator, Success measure, Achievement benchmark, Evaluation standard. Examples: Record Quarterly Operating Profits, Best Quarterly Performance, Tech Sector Record, Strong Performance.

chosen_type.label: PerformanceMetric
chosen_type.definition: A standard of measurement used to evaluate the effectiveness or success of an action, process, or entity.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class directly represents a general performance metric. QuantitativeValue is the closest parent as these are measurable values.

candidates.label: EmployerAggregateRating
candidates.comment: An EmployerAggregateRating is an AggregateRating representing a collective assessment of an Organization's performance as an employer. Also called company rating, employer review score, workplace satisfaction rating. Examples: Glassdoor's overall rating for a company, an average employee satisfaction score, a composite rating from multiple employee surveys.

candidates.label: MedicalRiskScore
candidates.comment: A medical risk estimator that is a simple system summing risk factors to yield a score associated with prognosis. Also called clinical score, prognostic score, risk index. Examples: "CHAD score", "TIMI risk score", "APACHE II score". Distinct from MedicalRiskCalculator, which involves more complex mathematical calculations.

candidates.label: EnergyEfficiencyEnumeration
candidates.comment: An EnergyEfficiencyEnumeration is an Enumeration of energy efficiency levels and certifications from various international standards. Also called energy rating, efficiency class, energy certification. Examples: EUEnergyEfficiencyEnumeration, EnergyStarEnergyEfficiencyEnumeration.

candidates.label: MeasurementMethodEnum
candidates.comment: An enumeration of methods used for measurement. Also called measurement technique, gauging method, assessment approach. Examples: "manual measurement", "automated sensor measurement", "self-reported measurement".

candidates.label: Certification
candidates.comment: An official and authoritative statement attesting to specific characteristics of a subject, issued by an independent body. Also called accreditation, credential, attestation, endorsement. Examples: ISO 9001 certification, Organic food certification, PMP certification, LEED certification.

types.embedding_query_text: OrganizationCategory: A grouping of organizations based on shared characteristics, industry, or function. Also called Industry sector, Business group, Corporate segment, Organizational class. Examples: Major South Korean Firms, Memory Companies, Rival Asian Firms.

chosen_type.label: OrganizationCategory
chosen_type.definition: A grouping of organizations based on shared characteristics, industry, or function.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class directly represents a general category or grouping of organizations. DefinedTerm is a suitable parent for a classification term.

candidates.label: Organization
candidates.comment: An Organization is a group of people with a particular purpose, such as a school, NGO, corporation, or club. Also called entity, institution, association. Examples: Google, Harvard University, Red Cross, a local sports club. Distinct from Person, which is an individual.

candidates.label: SportsOrganization
candidates.comment: A general category for organizations involved in sports, including teams, governing bodies, and associations. Also called athletic organization, sports body, sports group. Examples: the NBA, a local youth soccer league, the International Olympic Committee.

candidates.label: Consortium
candidates.comment: A membership organization typically composed of other organizations collaborating on a shared project or goal. Also called alliance, syndicate, federation, partnership. Examples: World Wide Web Consortium (W3C), a research consortium, a banking consortium, a joint venture. Distinct from Organization, which is a general grouping of people or entities.

candidates.label: SearchRescueOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization dedicated to finding and providing aid to people who are lost or in imminent danger. Also called SAR team, rescue service, emergency search unit. Examples: a mountain rescue team, a coast guard search and rescue unit, a volunteer SAR group.

candidates.label: LocalBusiness
candidates.comment: A specific physical business or a branch of an organization that serves a local community. Also called local company, neighborhood business, regional enterprise. Examples: a local restaurant, a bank branch, a medical clinic, a bowling alley, a grocery store. Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any group of people with a particular purpose.

types.embedding_query_text: DocumentType: A classification of written or recorded information based on its purpose, content, or format. Also called Report type, Record category, Publication kind, Information format. Examples: Official Detailed Reports, Earnings Forecast, Full Results, Investment Plans.

chosen_type.label: DocumentType
chosen_type.definition: A classification of written or recorded information based on its purpose, content, or format.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class directly represents a general classification of documents. DefinedTerm is a suitable parent for a classification term.

candidates.label: DataType
candidates.comment: DataType is a fundamental classification for the kind of values that can be stored or manipulated, such as numbers, text, or booleans. Also called primitive type, data format, value type. Examples: Integer, String, Boolean, Float, Date.

candidates.label: BookFormatType
candidates.comment: An Enumeration representing the physical or digital publication format of a book. Also called book edition type, publication format, reading format. Examples: "Hardcover", "Paperback", "Ebook", "Audiobook".

candidates.label: BusinessEntityType
candidates.comment: A BusinessEntityType is an Enumeration representing the legal form, size, main line of business, or position in the value chain of an organization or business person. Also called legal entity type, company structure, business classification. Examples: Corporation, Sole Proprietorship, Partnership, Non-profit Organization.

candidates.label: PurchaseType
candidates.comment: PurchaseType is an Enumeration listing different types of purchases for an item. Also called buying type, acquisition method. Examples: outright purchase, subscription, rental, lease.

candidates.label: DigitalDocumentPermissionType
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing a specific type of permission that can be granted for accessing a digital document. Also called Access level, permission role, document access type. Examples: ReadPermission, WritePermission, SharePermission, CommentPermission. Distinct from DigitalDocumentPermission, which is an instance of a permission granted to a specific entity.

types.embedding_query_text: Role: The function or position that someone has in a particular organization, event, or society. Also called Position, Function, Capacity, Part. Examples: Investors.

chosen_type.label: Role
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org Role class directly matches the OIE_TYPE definition, as 'Investors' describes a function or position.

candidates.label: Role
candidates.comment: Additional information describing a relationship or property, such as a person's function in an organization or a character played in a movie. Also called function, capacity, position, part. Examples: 'actor' role for a person in a film, 'member' role for a player on a sports team, 'author' role for a person on a book.

candidates.label: OrganizationRole
candidates.comment: An OrganizationRole, as a Role, describes a specific function or position within an organization. Also called organizational position, corporate role, job title. Examples: CEO, Marketing Manager, Board Member, Volunteer Coordinator. Distinct from Role, which is a broader category for any role.

candidates.label: PerformanceRole
candidates.comment: A PerformanceRole, as a Role, is a role an entity plays in a theatrical performance, such as a movie or TV series. Also called acting role, character role, stage role. Examples: 'actor in a film', 'director of a play', 'musician in a concert'. Distinct from OrganizationRole, which is a role within an organization.

candidates.label: EmployeeRole
candidates.comment: An EmployeeRole is an OrganizationRole describing the relationship of an individual as an employee within an organization. Also called job position, staff role, employment status. Examples: "Software Engineer" at Google, "Marketing Manager" at a startup, "Cashier" at a supermarket.

candidates.label: Date

candidates.label: Duration
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Duration represents a period of time, typically expressed in ISO 8601 format. Also called time span, period, length of time. Examples: "PT1H30M" (1 hour 30 minutes), "P3D" (3 days), "PT2H" (2 hours).

candidates.label: Season
candidates.comment: A distinct period within a media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called media season, series installment, broadcast season. Examples: 'Season 1 of Game of Thrones', 'The Fall 2023 radio season', 'Chapter 3 of a video game series'. Distinct from TVSeason, which is specifically for television broadcasts.

types.embedding_query_text: Quarter: A three-month period, often used for financial reporting. Also called Fiscal quarter, Trimester, Quarterly period, Reporting period. Examples: Q2 2026, Q2 2025, Q1 2026, the quarter.

types.embedding_query_text: Person: An individual human being. Also called Individual, Human, Man, Woman. Examples: Marc Einstein, Bryan Ma, industry analyst Marc Einstein, tech devices researcher Bryan Ma.

candidates.label: IndividualProduct
candidates.comment: An IndividualProduct is a single, identifiable instance of a product. Also called specific product unit, unique item, serialized product. Examples: Dr. Jane Smith (a family doctor), Dr. John Doe (a cardiologist), a local pediatrician. Distinct from Physician, which is the general role, and MedicalOrganization, which is a facility.

candidates.label: Researcher
candidates.comment: A Researcher is an Audience type representing individuals engaged in scientific or academic inquiry. Also called scientist, academic, scholar. Examples: a university professor, a lab scientist, a PhD student, an independent scholar.

candidates.label: Thing
candidates.comment: The most generic and fundamental type in schema.org, representing any item or entity. Also called entity, item, object. Examples: a person, a book, a place, an event.

types.embedding_query_text: Industry: A group of businesses that produce similar goods or services. Also called Sector, Business field, Trade, Market. Examples: Memory Industry.

chosen_type.label: Industry
chosen_type.definition: A group of businesses that produce similar goods or services.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class directly represents the concept of an 'Industry'. An industry is fundamentally a collective of organizations, making Organization a suitable parent.

candidates.label: SomeProducts
candidates.comment: A placeholder representing multiple similar products of the same kind, used when specific individual products are not distinguished. Also called product group, product category, generic products, similar items. Examples: 'a batch of apples', 'several identical t-shirts', 'a collection of standard screws'.

candidates.label: LocalBusiness
candidates.comment: A specific physical business or a branch of an organization that serves a local community. Also called local company, neighborhood business, regional enterprise. Examples: a local restaurant, a bank branch, a medical clinic, a bowling alley, a grocery store. Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any group of people with a particular purpose.

candidates.label: SportsActivityLocation
candidates.comment: A local business or facility providing a venue for sports activities. Also called sports venue, athletic facility, recreation center, playing field. Examples: a local gym, a public tennis court, a community swimming pool, a golf course.

candidates.label: BusinessEvent
candidates.comment: A BusinessEvent is an Event related to commercial activities, such as conferences, trade shows, or corporate meetings. Also called corporate event, professional gathering, industry event. Examples: a sales conference, a product launch event, an annual shareholder meeting. Distinct from SocialEvent, which is for personal or recreational gatherings.

candidates.label: EntertainmentBusiness
candidates.comment: An EntertainmentBusiness is a LocalBusiness that provides entertainment services. Also called amusement business, leisure provider. Examples: A movie theater, a concert venue, an arcade, a theme park.

types.embedding_query_text: Year: A period of 365 or 366 days, divided into 12 months, starting from January 1st. Also called Calendar year, Annual period, Fiscal year, Twelvemonth. Examples: Next Year.

chosen_type.label: Duration
chosen_type.justification: A year is a specific period of time, which aligns with the definition of schema.org Duration.

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

candidates.label: Season
candidates.comment: A distinct period within a media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called media season, series installment, broadcast season. Examples: 'Season 1 of Game of Thrones', 'The Fall 2023 radio season', 'Chapter 3 of a video game series'. Distinct from TVSeason, which is specifically for television broadcasts.

candidates.label: CreativeWorkSeason
candidates.comment: A CreativeWorkSeason is a distinct period or installment within a larger media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called TV season, media season, series season, broadcast season. Examples: "Game of Thrones Season 8," "The Crown Season 4," "The Mandalorian Season 2." Distinct from CreativeWorkSeries, which is the entire collection of seasons or related works.

candidates.label: Duration
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Duration represents a period of time, typically expressed in ISO 8601 format. Also called time span, period, length of time. Examples: "PT1H30M" (1 hour 30 minutes), "P3D" (3 days), "PT2H" (2 hours).

candidates.label: TVSeason
candidates.comment: A distinct period of a television series, comprising multiple episodes, dedicated to TV broadcast and associated online delivery. Also called television season, broadcast season, show season. Examples: 'Season 1 of The Crown', 'The final season of Breaking Bad'. Distinct from Season, which is a more general media season.

types.embedding_query_text: FacilityType: A classification of a place or building designed for a particular purpose. Also called Building type, Venue category, Site classification, Infrastructure type. Examples: AI Data Centres, Chip Factories.

chosen_type.label: FacilityType
chosen_type.definition: A classification of a place or building designed for a particular purpose.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class directly represents a general classification of facility types. DefinedTerm is a suitable parent for a classification term.

candidates.label: CivicStructure
candidates.comment: A public structure or building intended for public use or government functions. Also called public building, municipal structure, community facility. Examples: A library, a concert hall, a town hall, a park.

candidates.label: DefenceEstablishment
candidates.comment: A government building or civic structure primarily used for military or national defense purposes. Also called Military base, army base, naval base, air force station. Examples: The Pentagon, Fort Bragg, Pearl Harbor Naval Shipyard, Royal Air Force Lakenheath. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.

candidates.label: StadiumOrArena
candidates.comment: A large civic structure designed for sporting events, concerts, or other large-scale public gatherings. Also called stadium, arena, coliseum, sports complex. Examples: Wembley Stadium, Madison Square Garden, the Roman Colosseum.

candidates.label: House
candidates.comment: A House is an accommodation type representing a building or structure intended for human or other creature habitation. Also called dwelling, residence, home. Examples: a single-family home, a townhouse, a cottage. Distinct from Apartment, which is a unit within a larger building, and HotelRoom, which is a temporary lodging unit.

candidates.label: UKNonprofitType
candidates.comment: An enumeration of specific non-profit organization types recognized within the United Kingdom. Also called UK charity type, British non-profit category, UK voluntary sector classification. Examples: a registered charity, a community interest company (CIC), a benevolent society.

types.embedding_query_text: FinancialInstrument: A monetary contract between parties that can be created, traded, modified, and settled. Also called Security, Investment, Asset, Stock. Examples: Shares of Major Tech Firms, Samsung Shares, Nvidia Stock, Samsung's shares.

chosen_type.label: FinancialProduct
chosen_type.justification: Shares and stock are types of financial products, making schema.org FinancialProduct a good general fit for 'FinancialInstrument'.

candidates.label: FinancialIncentive
candidates.comment: A FinancialIncentive is an Intangible representing financial benefits offered for goods or services, including details like amount, status, and eligibility criteria. Also called rebate, subsidy, grant, discount. Examples: A government tax credit for electric vehicles, a manufacturer's rebate on an appliance, a low-interest loan program, a student scholarship.

candidates.label: InvestmentOrDeposit
candidates.comment: An InvestmentOrDeposit is a financial product service that typically requires a client to transfer funds to a financial service in return for potential beneficial financial returns. Also called financial investment, savings product, capital placement. Examples: a savings account, a certificate of deposit (CD), a stock market investment. Distinct from InvestmentFund, which is a specific type of pooled investment, and LoanOrCredit, which involves borrowing.

candidates.label: FinancialProduct
candidates.comment: A FinancialProduct is a Service provided by financial institutions to consumers and businesses. Also called financial instrument, banking product, investment product. Examples: A savings account, a mortgage loan, an insurance policy, a mutual fund.

candidates.label: MonetaryAmount
candidates.comment: A structured value representing a monetary value or range, typically expressed with a currency. Also called amount of money, financial value, currency amount. Examples: "$50 USD", "£1,000 to £1,000,000 GBP", "€25.99". Distinct from PriceSpecification, which describes the price of an offer.

candidates.label: PaymentService
candidates.comment: A PaymentService, as a FinancialProduct, is a service to transfer funds between persons or organizations. Also called money transfer service, payment processing service, remittance service. Examples: PayPal, Western Union, a bank's wire transfer service. Distinct from BankAccount, which is an account, not a service.

types.embedding_query_text: City: A large and densely populated urban area. Also called Metropolis, Town, Urban center, Municipality. Examples: Seoul.

chosen_type.label: City
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org City class directly matches the OIE_TYPE definition and 'Seoul' is a clear example of a city.

candidates.label: City
candidates.comment: A large and permanent human settlement, typically an administrative area with a defined government. Also called town, municipality, urban area, metropolis. Examples: New York City, London, Tokyo, Paris. Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a broader category including states, provinces, etc.

candidates.label: CityHall
candidates.comment: A government building serving as the administrative headquarters for a city or town. Also called town hall, municipal building, civic center. Examples: New York City Hall, London City Hall, a local town's municipal office. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.

candidates.label: StadiumOrArena
candidates.comment: A large civic structure designed for sporting events, concerts, or other large-scale public gatherings. Also called stadium, arena, coliseum, sports complex. Examples: Wembley Stadium, Madison Square Garden, the Roman Colosseum.

candidates.label: Zoo
candidates.comment: A civic structure and facility where wild animals are housed, exhibited, and often bred for conservation and public education. Also called zoological garden, animal park, wildlife park. Examples: San Diego Zoo, London Zoo, Bronx Zoo.

candidates.label: SubwayStation
candidates.comment: A civic structure serving as a stop or terminal for subway or metro trains. Also called metro station, underground station, tube station. Examples: 'Grand Central Terminal', 'London Underground station', 'Tokyo Metro station'.

types.embedding_query_text: FinancialIndex: A statistical measure of change in a stock market or economy, representing the performance of a group of assets. Also called Stock index, Market index, Benchmark index, Economic indicator. Examples: Kospi, South Korea's benchmark share index, the Kospi.

chosen_type.label: FinancialIndex
chosen_type.definition: A statistical measure of change in a stock market or economy, representing the performance of a group of assets.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class specifically represents a financial index. QuantitativeValue is the closest parent as it is a measurable statistical value.

candidates.label: FinancialIncentive
candidates.comment: A FinancialIncentive is an Intangible representing financial benefits offered for goods or services, including details like amount, status, and eligibility criteria. Also called rebate, subsidy, grant, discount. Examples: A government tax credit for electric vehicles, a manufacturer's rebate on an appliance, a low-interest loan program, a student scholarship.

candidates.label: ExchangeRateSpecification
candidates.comment: An ExchangeRateSpecification is a StructuredValue representing details about an exchange rate. Also called currency exchange rate, foreign exchange rate. Examples: The exchange rate between USD and EUR, a specific conversion rate for a financial transaction, details including fees and validity period.

candidates.label: MedicalRiskScore
candidates.comment: A medical risk estimator that is a simple system summing risk factors to yield a score associated with prognosis. Also called clinical score, prognostic score, risk index. Examples: "CHAD score", "TIMI risk score", "APACHE II score". Distinct from MedicalRiskCalculator, which involves more complex mathematical calculations.

candidates.label: InvestmentOrDeposit
candidates.comment: An InvestmentOrDeposit is a financial product service that typically requires a client to transfer funds to a financial service in return for potential beneficial financial returns. Also called financial investment, savings product, capital placement. Examples: a savings account, a certificate of deposit (CD), a stock market investment. Distinct from InvestmentFund, which is a specific type of pooled investment, and LoanOrCredit, which involves borrowing.

candidates.label: BankAccount
candidates.comment: A FinancialProduct or service offered by a bank for depositing, withdrawing, or transferring money, often with interest. Also called bank account, checking account, savings account, deposit account. Examples: "My personal checking account", "A business savings account", "A joint current account".

types.embedding_query_text: Country: A nation with its own government, occupying a particular territory. Also called Nation, State, Land, Realm. Examples: South Korea, Japan, China, Taiwan.

chosen_type.label: Country
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org Country class directly matches the OIE_TYPE definition and all mentions are sovereign nations.

candidates.label: Country
candidates.comment: A Country is a sovereign state or nation, representing a primary administrative division of the Earth's surface. Also called nation, state, sovereign state, realm. Examples: United States, Canada, France, Japan, Brazil.

candidates.label: State
candidates.comment: A major administrative division of a country, such as a state or province. Also called province, region, territory, commonwealth. Examples: California, Ontario, Bavaria, Texas.

candidates.label: DefenceEstablishment
candidates.comment: A government building or civic structure primarily used for military or national defense purposes. Also called Military base, army base, naval base, air force station. Examples: The Pentagon, Fort Bragg, Pearl Harbor Naval Shipyard, Royal Air Force Lakenheath. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.

candidates.label: SingleFamilyResidence
candidates.comment: A type of house designed to be occupied by one family, typically detached from other homes. Also called detached house, single-family home, private residence. Examples: a suburban house with a yard, a standalone cottage, a bungalow.

candidates.label: BodyOfWater
candidates.comment: A Landform representing a significant accumulation of water, such as a sea, ocean, or lake. Also called aquatic environment, water body, large water mass. Examples: "The Pacific Ocean", "Lake Superior", "The Mediterranean Sea", "The Nile River". Distinct from Beach, which is a specific landform adjacent to a body of water.

types.embedding_query_text: FinancialActivity: An action or process related to the management of money, banking, investments, and credit. Also called Monetary transaction, Fiscal operation, Investment activity, Economic action. Examples: Investments.

chosen_type.label: FinancialActivity
chosen_type.definition: An action or process related to the management of money, banking, investments, and credit.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class directly represents a general 'FinancialActivity'. Action is the most appropriate parent for a type of action.

candidates.label: TradeAction
candidates.comment: The act of exchanging goods or services for monetary compensation. Also called commerce, transaction, selling. Examples: a business selling products to customers, a consultant providing services for a fee, an artist selling their artwork.

candidates.label: InvestmentOrDeposit
candidates.comment: An InvestmentOrDeposit is a financial product service that typically requires a client to transfer funds to a financial service in return for potential beneficial financial returns. Also called financial investment, savings product, capital placement. Examples: a savings account, a certificate of deposit (CD), a stock market investment. Distinct from InvestmentFund, which is a specific type of pooled investment, and LoanOrCredit, which involves borrowing.

candidates.label: FinancialIncentive
candidates.comment: A FinancialIncentive is an Intangible representing financial benefits offered for goods or services, including details like amount, status, and eligibility criteria. Also called rebate, subsidy, grant, discount. Examples: A government tax credit for electric vehicles, a manufacturer's rebate on an appliance, a low-interest loan program, a student scholarship.

candidates.label: MoneyTransfer
candidates.comment: The action of transferring money from one place to another, either electronically or physically. Also called fund transfer, wire transfer, remittance, cash transfer. Examples: sending money via a banking app, wiring funds internationally, handing over cash. Distinct from TransferAction, which is a broader category for moving any object.

candidates.label: FinancialService
candidates.comment: A FinancialService is a LocalBusiness that provides financial services. Also called bank, credit union, investment firm, insurance company. Examples: A retail bank, a wealth management firm, an insurance agency, a loan provider.

types.embedding_query_text: Project: A planned piece of work that has a specific purpose and that usually requires a lot of time and effort. Also called Undertaking, Initiative, Task, Venture. Examples: Projects.

chosen_type.label: Project
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org Project class directly matches the OIE_TYPE definition and 'Projects' is a clear example.

candidates.label: Project
candidates.comment: A Project is an Organization representing an enterprise, typically collaborative, planned to achieve a particular aim. Also called initiative, endeavor, venture. Examples: a software development project, a construction project, a research initiative, a community outreach program.

candidates.label: ResearchProject
candidates.comment: A ResearchProject is a Project representing a planned enterprise aimed at scientific or academic inquiry. Also called research initiative, study, academic project. Examples: a clinical trial, a grant-funded scientific study, a historical research project, a university-led exploration.

candidates.label: Conversation
candidates.comment: A series of one or more messages exchanged between individuals or organizations on a specific topic. Also called discussion, dialogue, chat, discourse. Examples: An email thread, a text message exchange, a forum discussion, a spoken dialogue. Distinct from Comment, which is a single remark on an item.

candidates.label: Review
candidates.comment: A critical assessment or evaluation of an item, such as a product, service, or creative work. Also called critique, appraisal, rating, feedback. Examples: a movie review on Rotten Tomatoes, a restaurant review on Yelp, a product review on Amazon, a book review in a newspaper.

candidates.label: Diet
candidates.comment: A creative work outlining a strategy for regulating food intake to achieve a specific health or fitness goal. Also called Eating plan, nutritional regimen, dietary program, meal plan. Examples: The Mediterranean diet, a ketogenic diet, a low-sodium diet, a vegan diet. Distinct from NutritionInformation, which provides factual data about food content.

types.embedding_query_text: IndustrySector: A segment of an economy that shares common characteristics, such as products, services, or business models. Also called Economic sector, Market segment, Business area, Industrial segment. Examples: Chip Manufacturing, country's chip manufacturing.

chosen_type.label: IndustrySector
chosen_type.definition: A broad classification of businesses based on the primary economic activity they engage in.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class directly represents an 'IndustrySector'. DefinedTerm is a suitable parent for a classification term.

candidates.label: MedicalRiskFactor
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing anything that increases a person's likelihood of developing a disease, medical condition, or complication. Also called risk element, predisposing factor, vulnerability. Examples: "smoking", "high cholesterol", "family history of heart disease", "obesity". Distinct from MedicalRiskEstimator, which is a tool to calculate risk based on multiple factors.

candidates.label: MemberProgramTier
candidates.comment: An intangible representing a specific tier within a loyalty or membership program. Also called membership level, loyalty tier, program status. Examples: "Gold Member", "Platinum Tier", "Basic Membership Level".

candidates.label: ProductModel
candidates.comment: A ProductModel is a Product representing a datasheet or vendor specification of a prototypical product description. Also called product prototype, product specification, product blueprint. Examples: the technical specifications for a new laptop model, a design document for a car engine, a vendor's product data sheet, a conceptual product design.

candidates.label: SomeProducts
candidates.comment: A placeholder representing multiple similar products of the same kind, used when specific individual products are not distinguished. Also called product group, product category, generic products, similar items. Examples: 'a batch of apples', 'several identical t-shirts', 'a collection of standard screws'.

candidates.label: BusinessEntityType
candidates.comment: A BusinessEntityType is an Enumeration representing the legal form, size, main line of business, or position in the value chain of an organization or business person. Also called legal entity type, company structure, business classification. Examples: Corporation, Sole Proprietorship, Partnership, Non-profit Organization.
